title: On‑Prem Network Escalation Lifecycle and Prioritization Criteria for Air‑Gapped/Private Requests
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: Create a repeatable escalation lifecycle and prioritization rubric for customer requests that touch networking, upgrades, and air‑gapped constraints for Private/VPC/on‑prem deployments. This ticket scopes the policy, intake surface, decision gates, and artifacts required to safely fast‑track low‑risk requests while ensuring high‑risk changes follow an operator runbook.
goals: 1) Reduce time-to-first-response for network-related onprem requests from intake to plan within 3 business days for low/medium risk. 2) Define deterministic prioritization buckets and acceptance criteria for fastlane vs operator lanes. 3) Provide a standardized intake manifest and probe checklist customers can run to self-validate connectivity and upgrade compatibility. 4) Identify automation opportunities (preflight probes, scoring).
background_and_problem_statement: We consistently see long lead times when customers request network exceptions, egress windows, or rolling upgrade assistance for air‑gapped/on‑prem deployments. Lack of standardized signals leads to back-and-forth clarifications, missed windows, and ad hoc escalations that overload Solutions and SRE. Existing playbooks cover many edge cases but are fragmented; teams want a single lifecycle and scorecard to route requests into correct engagement lanes.
proposal: 1) Define a 4‑step lifecycle: Intake -> Preflight -> Risk Score -> Engagement Lane. 2) Intake: new self-serve manifest (YAML) that captures topology, egress policy, upgrade cadence, FW/Proxy constraints, and testing endpoints. 3) Preflight: customer-run probe bundle (curl/ssh/ICMP/egress handshake) that uploads a signed report to our intake service. 4) Risk Score: deterministic rubric (0-100) using signals: egress scope, exposure, maintenance window flexibility, business criticality, regulatory constraints, and past audit history. 5) Engagement lanes: Fastlane (score < 25, automated approval + runbook), Assisted (score 25-60, SRE + Solutions), Escalation (score > 60, security review + cross-functional steering).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Draft rubric published and reviewed by Solutions, SRE, Security, and Legal. 2) Example intake manifest and preflight probe bundle available in the private-deploy docs. 3) Three customer playbook templates (fastlane, assisted, escalation) with expected SLA/response times. 4) Pilot with 4 existing enterprise customers and measurable reduction in clarification cycles (target: -40% clarifying questions).
out_of_scope: Building full automation into the Console intake API (we will prototype CLI + signed report upload only). On‑prem agent deployment packaging is out of scope for this ticket.
stakeholders: PM: Maya Patel; Eng Owners: Evan Morales (Solutions), Priya Rao (SRE); Security: Noah Chen; Legal: Susan Blake; Customer Success: Lina Torres; Sales Eng: Karim Haddad
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly permissive fastlane could enable insecure config changes. Mitigation: Fastlane only for narrow egress/maintenance-window requests, signed probe evidence required, circuit-breaker to revoke approvals. Risk: Customers unable to run probes due to strict airgap. Mitigation: Provide operator-assisted probe intake and a manual evidence collection checklist.
deliverables: 1) Prioritization rubric doc (Confluence link). 2) Intake manifest schema (YAML example). 3) Preflight probe CLI bundle and upload endpoint (prototype). 4) Runbooks for Fastlane/Assisted/Escalation lanes. 5) Pilot report and run-rate metrics dashboard.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Draft rubric and manifest schema, align with Security + SRE. Week 2: Build probe bundle PoC and intake upload endpoint; create runbook drafts. Week 3: Internal review and tabletop exercises with support and solutions. Week 4: Customer pilot with 4 customers; collect feedback and iterate. Post-pilot: handoff to Console/product team for API intake and automation in Q2.
open_questions: 1) What minimum signed evidence format satisfies Legal for audit? 2) How do we surface runbook state in Console without full API work? 3) Which customer segments get pilot invites (sales-qualified vs self-serve)?
